description.narrative:
The project target group are small-holders farmers in Mali and Nigeria facing cascading crisis of insecurity, climate change and biodiversity loss. The project focuses on locations that are highly vulnerable, remote, heavily affected by climate change and violentconflicts, and people often struggle to cover basic needs, which leads to dependency on emergency aid. Both men and women farmers will be targeted, with particular focus on engaging young farmers. Through this project an estimated 1200 smallholder farmers will besupported, indirectly benefiting approximately 10,000 households indirectly. Between 40 percent of participating farmers will be women, and 20 percent youth. For smallholder farmers, seed is the most fundamental resource, access to high-quality, diverse seeds is essential for:
- Enhancing crop productivity and agricultural biodiversity - Improving food and nutrition security - Strengthening resilience to climate change - Ensuring livelihood continuity season after season
By engaging farmers in seed production at community level the project provides sustainable access to good-quality diverse seeds for enhanced agricultural productivity, food and nutrition security.
Project activities and outcomes are:
- Improved seed supply in project sites through community level seed production - Providing a diversity of crops and varieties to farmers to enable them to cope better with climate change. - Livelihood diversification resulting in increased household income for farmers in Mali and Nigeria. - Well trained and competent small-scale seed entrepreneurs including women and youth - Linkages with seed value chain actors (to the extent possible in fragile contexts) - Customizethe Farmer Field School training material - Reduced dependency on seed aid within the community - Advocate for local farmers to be seed suppliers of choice where seed aid cannot be avoided. - And ultimately foster the much-needed social cohesion in the context ofunrest through meeting the essential need for food in a setting that fosters collaboration and working in solidarity.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam is an international confederation of 17 organizations working together in more than 90 countries. Oxfam International was formed in 1995 by a group of independent non-governmental organizations. Their aim was to work together for greater impact on the international stage to reduce poverty and injustice. The name "Oxfam" comes from the Oxford Committee for Famine Relief, founded in Britain in 1942. The group campaigned for food supplies to be sent through an allied naval blockade to starving women and children in enemy-occupied Greece during the Second World War.As well as becoming a world leader in the delivery of emergency relief, Oxfam International implements long-term development programs in vulnerable communities. We are also part of a global movement, campaigning with others, for instance, to end unfair trade rules, demand better health and education services for all, and to combat climate change. Today, there are 17 member organizations of the Oxfam International confederation. They are based in: Australia, Belgium, Canada,France, Germany, Great Britain, Hong Kong, Ireland, India, Italy, Japan, Mexico, The Netherlands, New Zealand, Quebec, Spain and the United States. The Oxfam International Secretariat is based in Oxford, UK. The Secretariat runs advocacy offices in Brussels, Geneva, New York, Washington DC and Brasilia. Oxfam GB is an actor in the implementation of this project.....
